definition: Underrepresentation means the state of having fewer members or less presence than a fair share.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word underrepresentation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know underrepresentation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The atlas's underrepresentation of the southern hemisphere was literal: forty pages north of the equator, nine below it.
An imbalance is milder than underrepresentation — any tilt in the numbers, often accidental and small; underrepresentation is a tilt deep enough to cost a group its fair share of presence.
Exclusion goes further than underrepresentation — underrepresentation leaves a group thin in the room; exclusion leaves the group outside the door entirely.

A shortfall is any gap between what should be there and what is — budgets, harvests, and donations all have shortfalls. Underrepresentation is a shortfall specifically of presence: a group holding fewer seats, pages, or voices than its real share. Every underrepresentation is a shortfall of one particular kind.

An undercount is a tally that misses part of the group — a counting error, a survey that never reached them. Underrepresentation can exist with a perfect count: everyone tallied accurately, and the group still holding less presence than its share. An undercount hides people; underrepresentation seats too few of them.

For its spring issue, the student paper measured the yearbook instead of writing about it.
The three sports teams, with ninety members among them, filled thirty-one pages of photographs; the six arts clubs, with a hundred and forty members, shared four.
The editors were careful to say the yearbook staff had missed no one — every club roster appeared, every member was named in the index.
The underrepresentation was in the space itself: more students belonged to the arts clubs, yet they held barely an eighth of the pages given to sports.
The yearbook adviser promised the next edition would divide its pages by membership, not by tradition.
